messages.subject: Re: [poppr] poppr as 'translator'?
parts:
Hi Emily,

I've seen this kind of request a couple of times recently, and I realized that currently there's no built-in way for converting data to polysat. I've written a function a while ago and posted it to the adegenet forum recently (http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/adegenet-forum/2018-February/001752.html). You may wish to check it out (https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/aeaff83b9d126d55aade). I am moving toward a release of a new version of poppr within the next month and I think I will include conversion functions for polysat. 

Regarding your problem here:

I cannot get poppr to pick up my GenAlEx file at all. 

There's not much we can do without more information. It would be helpful if you could copy and paste the error message you get (even better: use it to search google) along with the results of the sessionInfo() command. 

Hope that helps.
Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology
University of Nebraska-Lincoln
ORCID: 0000-0003-1458-7108




On Mar 2, 2018, at 21:30 , Emily Gillespie <emilylg...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello,

I am very new to R. I know that I ultimately need to use Polysat to analyze my tetraploid microsatellite data. I am very familiar with the GenAlEx plugin for diploid data. I am having trouble getting my data into a format that can be read by Polysat, and I read that poppr includes the ability to read GenAlEx-formatted files. I am hoping that I can then export the file as a genemapper-formatted file, since I know how to do basic analyses with that kind of file in Polysat. My GenAlEx file is formatted exactly as the GenAlEx manual stipulates, except that there are four columns for each locus, and like here: http://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Data_Preparation.html  under 'Polyploids'. Yet I cannot read in the file.

1) Is this possible (using poppr as a 'go between' from GenAlEx to genemapper? If so, 2) my next problem is that I cannot get poppr to pick up my GenAlEx file at all. I suspect it is something basic because I am so new to R. Any help is appreciated.

--

parts: The next version of poppr will include a new function called as.genambig, which will perform the conversion from genind to genambig format. If you want to try it out, you can install poppr from the github page or wait about a week :)
